blocks.prompt: 20. If \(a_1, a_2, a_3, \ldots, a_n\) are positive and in A.P., prove that \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{a_1} + \sqrt{a_2}} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{a_2} + \sqrt{a_3}} + \cdots + \frac{1}{\sqrt{a_{n-1}} + \sqrt{a_n}} = \frac{n - 1}{\sqrt{a_1} + \sqrt{a_n}}\).
blocks.explanation:
A proof with a long sum. Each fraction has a sum of two square roots at the bottom.
Rationalising each fraction makes its bottom equal to \(d\), and then the sum collapses (telescopes).
Plan: rationalise one general term, add all of them, then rewrite the result.
steps:
Given: \(a_1, \ldots, a_n\) positive, in A.P. with common difference \(d\)
To prove: L.H.S. \(= \dfrac{n - 1}{\sqrt{a_1} + \sqrt{a_n}}\).
Method: Rationalise; use \(a_{r+1} - a_r = d\) and \(a_n - a_1 = (n - 1)d\). First take \(d \ne 0\).

Rationalise a general term
\[\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{a_r} + \sqrt{a_{r+1}}}\]
\[= \dfrac{\sqrt{a_{r+1}} - \sqrt{a_r}}{a_{r+1} - a_r}\]
\[= \dfrac{\sqrt{a_{r+1}} - \sqrt{a_r}}{d}\]
Why: Multiply top and bottom by \(\sqrt{a_{r+1}} - \sqrt{a_r}\); the bottom becomes \((\sqrt{a_{r+1}})^2 - (\sqrt{a_r})^2\) because \((x + y)(y - x) = y^2 - x^2\), and neighbouring terms of an A.P. differ by \(d\).

Add all the terms
\[\text{L.H.S.} = \dfrac{1}{d}\big[(\sqrt{a_2} - \sqrt{a_1}) + (\sqrt{a_3} - \sqrt{a_2})\]
\[+ \cdots + (\sqrt{a_n} - \sqrt{a_{n-1}})\big]\]
\[= \dfrac{\sqrt{a_n} - \sqrt{a_1}}{d}\]
Why: Every middle root appears once with + and once with -, so only the first and last survive.

Rationalise again
\[= \dfrac{a_n - a_1}{d(\sqrt{a_1} + \sqrt{a_n})}\]
Why: The answer has \(\sqrt{a_1} + \sqrt{a_n}\) at the bottom, so multiply top and bottom by it; the top becomes \((\sqrt{a_n})^2 - (\sqrt{a_1})^2 = a_n - a_1\).

Use \(a_n - a_1 = (n - 1)d\)
\[= \dfrac{(n - 1)d}{d(\sqrt{a_1} + \sqrt{a_n})}\]
\[= \dfrac{n - 1}{\sqrt{a_1} + \sqrt{a_n}} = \text{R.H.S.}\]
Why: \(a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)d\); then \(d\) cancels.

The case \(d = 0\)
\[\text{L.H.S.} = (n - 1) \cdot \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{a_1}} = \text{R.H.S.}\]
Why: If \(d = 0\) all terms are equal; there are \(n - 1\) equal fractions and the right side is also \(\frac{n - 1}{2\sqrt{a_1}}\). So the result holds in every case.
